title: Servlet and URL Discrepancies in Security Filters
platform_conditions: Jakarta/Javax servlet containers (Tomcat, Jetty, Undertow); exact normalization differences depend on container version, which is why the review must confirm the container's rules
security_mechanism: A security filter that decides on getRequestURI() sees the RAW request path while the container later maps the SERVLET path after decoding and normalizing, so /admin;%2fadmin, //admin, /./admin, and %-encoded variants pass the prefix check yet land on the protected resource — the checker and the dispatcher disagree about which resource is being accessed. java.net.URL additionally treats a URL as a string with equals/openStream semantics differing from java.net.URI's RFC-3986 parsing (URL equals resolves hostnames via DNS, URI does not), and URL.openConnection dispatches on the scheme (file:, jar:, http:) so an attacker-controlled URL can pick the file handler; redirects and RequestDispatcher.forward re-enter the filter chain with a different path than the one originally checked.

source_sink_clues.source: Request paths, query strings, forward/include targets, and URLs taken from requests or configuration for outbound fetches.
source_sink_clues.sink: Security filters making allow/deny decisions on HttpServletRequest.getRequestURI() / getRequestURL() string prefixes; URL/URI comparisons guarding redirects or fetches; URL.openConnection on attacker-influenced URLs; forward/redirect targets validated only on the original path

tracking_guards: Require the decision be made on the container-decoded, normalized path (getServletPath/getPathInfo or the matched mapping) rather than the raw URI, and re-run the check after any forward; require URL allowlist checks on a canonicalized URI with the scheme fixed to https and redirect targets re-validated per hop; confirm container-level encoding rules with the actual container version.
not_candidate_when: Authorization is enforced at the resource/mapping level (container or framework security constraints) rather than by string prefixes on the raw URI, the path is decoded and normalized before comparison and re-checked after forwards, or the outbound URL's scheme and host are matched against a fixed allowlist on canonical form.
public_references: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/601.html
OWASP Authentication Cheat Sheet (authorization enforcement points) — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html
